_meta.description: Offline static intelligence for Marathahalli, Bengaluru. All facts are sourced from named authoritative public sources. Values estimated without direct measurement are marked with lower confidence.

bmtc._source: BMTC published route maps at bmtcinfo.com and DULT Bengaluru origin-destination survey 2022-23. Marathahalli is a major bus junction on the Outer Ring Road IT corridor.
bmtc._limitations: BMTC does not publish GTFS. Marathahalli serves as a transit junction but residential street penetration by BMTC is limited. Many IT workers use employer shuttles.
bmtc.routeCountNote: Approximate count of BMTC routes through or terminating at Marathahalli from DULT survey. Marathahalli is primarily a pass-through junction for ORR corridor routes rather than a route origin.

majorRoutes.description: Marathahalli – Kempegowda BS (Volvo AC via ORR)

bmtc.majorRoutesNote: Representative list only; verify at bmtcinfo.com. Most routes stop at Marathahalli Junction bus stop on ORR.

peakHeadwayMinutes.description: Typical peak-hour headway at Marathahalli Junction (ORR) bus stop

nammaMetro._source: BMRCL published Purple Line Phase 2A station list and alignment. No Namma Metro station exists within the Marathahalli OSM locality boundary. The nearest Purple Line stations are on the Whitefield extension.
nammaMetro._limitations: No operational metro station in Marathahalli as of July 2026. Nearest Purple Line stations are outside the Marathahalli locality boundary. Verify at bmrcl.co.in.
nammaMetro.line: Purple Line Phase 2A (nearest stations outside Marathahalli boundary)

nearbyStations.name: Brookefields / Hoodi (Purple Line Phase 2A)
nearbyStations.note: Nearest operational Purple Line station to Marathahalli; accessible by auto-rickshaw or BMTC feeder from Marathahalli junction

commuteDestinations._source: OpenStreetMap road network geometry; off-peak routing estimates via OSM topology
commuteDestinations._limitations: Drive times are indicative only. Outer Ring Road at Marathahalli is among the most congested stretches in Bengaluru during peak hours; peak times 3–5× off-peak.

water._source: BWSSB published zone maps and reports 2022-23; Karnataka Jal Jeevan Mission progress reports; media coverage on Mahadevapura water supply (Citizen Matters 2022-23)
water._license: Government public information; journalism attribution retained
water._limitations: BWSSB Cauvery pipeline coverage in Marathahalli is significantly limited. Most of the locality depends on groundwater borewells and tankers. Data from published reports.
water.authority: Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) — partial coverage
water.primaryWaterSource: Groundwater borewells (majority); Cauvery pipeline for BWSSB-connected buildings only
water.supplyFrequency: BWSSB piped supply where available: 2–3 days per week, 1 hour per cycle. Most of Marathahalli residential area depends on borewells or tankers.
water.boreholeStatus: Marathahalli has high borehole dependence. Groundwater levels have declined due to heavy IT and residential extraction. Tanker availability is constrained during summer.
water.sewageSystem: Limited BWSSB UGD; many properties use individual septic tanks or apartment STPs
water.notes: Marathahalli's water supply is among the less reliable in the BBMP area. BWSSB Cauvery Stage V project is extending coverage; pipeline connection rate currently estimated 25–40% of built properties. Source: BWSSB project status reports.

electricity._source: KERC Annual Performance Review 2023-24; BESCOM annual report 2022-23
electricity._limitations: SAIDI and SAIFI are BESCOM-zone aggregates.

ndvi._source: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance NDVI over Marathahalli polygon via Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. Analysis July 2024. Reference: Ramachandra et al. (2017) Bengaluru's growth and greening patterns, Current Science.
ndvi._license: Copernicus Sentinel data — free and open access under ESA Copernicus open data policy
ndvi._limitations: 10 m Sentinel-2 pixel; single dry-season composite. Marathahalli is predominantly a commercial junction with high impervious surface fraction. Seasonal variation ±0.07.
ndvi.ndviClassification: Low urban vegetation — predominantly commercial and transitional zone with high impervious surface fraction; among the lower NDVI localities in the Outer Ring Road corridor
ndvi.comparisonContext: Bengaluru urban NDVI average ~0.20–0.28 (Ranagaswamy & Devaraj 2019). Marathahalli is significantly below city average due to its heavy commercial development and absence of major parks or lakes within the OSM boundary.

heatIsland._source: Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature (Band 10); USGS Earth Explorer. Analysis comparing Marathahalli polygon to rural reference, May 2024. Reference: Ramachandra et al. (2017) Bengaluru UHI, Current Science Vol 113.
heatIsland._license: Landsat data is in the public domain (USGS/NASA)
heatIsland._limitations: 30 m Landsat thermal resolution. Surface temperature ≠ air temperature. Large asphalt ORR surface is a significant heat source.
heatIsland.uhiClassification: High urban heat island — commercial junction with large asphalt and concrete surfaces and minimal vegetation; among the higher UHI localities on the ORR corridor

ward._source: BBMP published ward delimitation 2022 (Mahadevapura Zone); Census of India 2011
ward.areaNote: Marathahalli is a relatively small locality (primarily the junction area and adjacent residential pockets). Ward 148 is the primary reference.
ward.populationNote: 2011 Census population; actual 2024 population substantially higher with IT corridor growth

complaints._source: BBMP Sahaaya grievance portal (FY 2022-23); iChangeMyCity; Citizen Matters ORR corridor reports 2022-24
complaints._license: Public grievance portal data; attribution retained
complaints._limitations: Complaint counts reflect only registered grievances. Marathahalli's transient commuter population may lower the effective complaint-registration rate relative to actual civic issues.

totalComplaintsPerYear.note: Approximate registered complaints for Marathahalli ward, FY 2022-23

topCategories.note: ORR service lanes and residential access roads near Marathahalli junction are frequently reported. Heavy goods vehicle movement damages interior roads.
Borewell failure and tanker non-availability are recurring complaints given limited BWSSB coverage.
Commercial establishments on ORR and residential apartments both contribute to waste management complaints.
Selected low-lying lanes adjacent to Doddakannelli nala flood during monsoon.
Marathahalli Bridge and ORR junction are identified traffic bottlenecks; multiple fatalities reported at the flyover intersection.

crime._source: NCRB Crime in India 2022 — Bengaluru City district-level; Karnataka SCRB Annual Report 2022
crime._limitations: Crime data available only at city/district level. No open ward-level crime breakdown exists for Marathahalli.
crime.localityNote: Marathahalli is served by Marathahalli Police Station. No public database provides FIR counts or crime rates at ward or locality level.

internet._source: TRAI Broadband Report Q4 2023-24; Ookla Speedtest Global Index Bengaluru Q4 2023; ACT Fibernet, Airtel, Jio Fiber public coverage maps
internet._license: TRAI: public regulatory data; Ookla: research citations permitted
internet._limitations: TRAI data is circle-level. Residential apartment complex coverage is generally good; standalone houses may have fewer options.
internet.fiberAvailability: Moderate-High — Marathahalli is served by major ISPs; IT park proximity drives good fiber infrastructure in the corridor

confirmedIsps.name: ACT Fibernet
confirmedIsps.coverageNote: Good coverage in Marathahalli residential areas
